p:cNvPr.descr: On the top left is inosine. It contains 2 rings, 1 6-sided and one 5-sided. The apical C on the 6-sided structure double bonds up to O, down and left to NH, which bonds down to C, which double bonds down and right to N. N bonds up and right to C, which double bonds up to C, which bonds up and left to C. Bonded to the right is the 5-sided structure. Its apical N double bonds down and right to C, which bonds down to N, which bonds down ro ribose (boxed) and left to C. C double bonds up to C, which bonds up and right to N. To the right is pseurouridine. It is a single 6-sided ring structure. Its apical C double bonds up to O, down and left to NH, which bonds down to C, which double bonds down and left to O and down and right to NH, which bonds up and right to C. C double bonds up to C, which bonds up and right to ribose (boxed) and up and left to the initial C. On the bottom left is 7-methylguanosine. The apical C of the 6-sided ring double bonds up to O, down and left to NH, which bonds down to C. C bonds down and left to NH2. C double bonds right to N, which bonds up and right to C. C double bonds up to C, which bonds up and left to the initial C. To the right, the apical N+ of the 5-sided ring double bonds down and right to C, which bonds down to N. N bonds down to ribose (boxed), left to C, which double bonds up to C, which bonds up and right to N. To the right is 4-thiouridine. It is a 6-sided ring structure. Its apical C double bonds up to S, down and left to NH, and down to C. C double bonds down and left to O, and down and right to N. N bonds down to ribose (boxed) and up and right to C. C double bonds up to C, which bonds up and left to the apical C.
